nodes.label: sequentially consistent
nodes.def: The strongest memory ordering requiring a single total order of all sequentially consistent operations visible to all threads; implied by default for std::atomic operations in C++.

nodes.label: c11 memory model
nodes.def: Standard C11 specification defining memory orderings: memory_order_relaxed, memory_order_consume, memory_order_acquire, memory_order_release, memory_order_acq_rel, memory_order_seq

nodes.label: exponential backoff
nodes.def: Contention management strategy backing off exponentially after failed lock acquisition; reduces bus traffic and collision; common in spinlock and CAS-based algorithm implementation

nodes.label: mcs lock
nodes.def: Queued lock where each waiting thread spins on a locally-owned node linked into a queue; cache-friendly with only O(1) bus traffic per lock acquisition; named after Mellor-Crummey

nodes.label: acquire semantics
nodes.def: Memory ordering semantics ensuring all subsequent loads/stores cannot be reordered before the acquire operation; used for lock acquisition, reading a flag after volatile write.

nodes.label: happens before relation
nodes.def: A fundamental ordering relation in memory models defining that if operation A happens-before operation B, then A's effects are visible to B; forms the basis for reasoning about pro

nodes.label: synchronizes with
nodes.def: A relation between atomic operations in memory models where a release fence on one thread synchronizes with an acquire fence on another thread, establishing happens-before order ac

nodes.label: atomic cas
nodes.def: Compare-and-swap operation atomically loading a value, comparing it to an expected value, and storing a new value only if they matched, returning whether the swap occurred.

nodes.label: bounded buffer
nodes.def: Classic synchronization problem with fixed-size buffer between producers and consumers; requires empty/full conditions and mutual exclusion; solution uses semaphores or monitors.

nodes.label: current delay
nodes.def: The computed wait interval for the current retry iteration; derived from base_delay multiplied by backoff_multiplier raised to the iteration count, then capped by delay_ceiling.

nodes.label: deadlock
nodes.def: Liveness failure where two or more threads wait indefinitely for conditions held by each other; occurs with circular wait, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and mutual exclusion.

nodes.label: hardware transactional memory htm
nodes.def: CPU-supported transactional execution using cache hierarchies to track conflicts; Intel TSX and IBM Blue Gene/Q implementations; aborts on cache conflict or unsupported instruction

nodes.label: jitter
nodes.def: Randomized variance introduced into the computed delay to decorrelate competing threads and mitigate thundering-herd synchronization on lock release.

nodes.label: mcs lock enqueue
nodes.def: Operation appending a thread-local qnode to the queue tail; atomically CASes qnode into tail; on CAS failure, completes the predecessor's link and retries; ensures FIFO acquisition

nodes.label: memory barrier
nodes.def: Instruction or hardware mechanism that prevents reordering of memory operations across the barrier; ensures visibility and ordering of loads and stores relative to the barrier poin

nodes.label: release semantics
nodes.def: Memory ordering semantics ensuring all prior loads/stores cannot be reordered after the release operation; used for lock release, writing data before a volatile flag.

nodes.label: spinlock
nodes.def: Lock implementation that spins in a tight loop waiting for acquisition; efficient when contention is brief but wasteful if held long; often implemented with atomic instructions.

nodes.label: atomic operation
nodes.def: Operation appearing indivisible to other threads; either hardware-supported single instruction atomics or software-implemented atomic primitives using CAS loops.

nodes.label: barrier synchronization
nodes.def: Primitive blocking threads until all threads in a set reach the barrier point; threads proceed only after the group is complete; used in fork-join and bulk-synchronous parallelism.

nodes.label: cache coherency
nodes.def: Protocol ensuring that multiple caches sharing a memory location present a consistent view; MESI, MOESI, MESIF protocols maintain coherence across CPU cores.

nodes.label: compare and swap cas
nodes.def: Atomic instruction comparing a value with expected and swaps only if equal; fundamental building block for lock-free algorithms; ABA problem may require additional solutions.

nodes.label: fork join parallelism
nodes.def: Parallelism pattern where work recursively splits into subtasks that join at barriers; implementations like Java ForkJoinFramework provide efficient work stealing for divide-conque

nodes.label: lock free
nodes.def: Progress guarantee where system-wide progress is always made; at least one thread completes an operation in finite steps regardless of other thread interference.

nodes.label: mcs lock qnode
nodes.def: Thread-local queue node containing locked flag and successor pointer; must be cache-aligned and allocated per-thread to enable local spinning without shared contention.

nodes.label: mcs lock release
nodes.def: Operation by which a thread releases the lock; sets own qnode.locked to false to unblock spinning successor; if successor exists in qnode.next, responsibility transfers to successo

nodes.label: memory reclamation
nodes.def: Challenge of safely reclaiming freed memory in lock-free structures accessed concurrently; solutions include hazard pointers, RCU, epoch-based reclamation, and quiescent-state-base

nodes.label: mutex
nodes.def: Mutual exclusion primitive providing exclusive access to a resource; supports lock/unlock operations and optionally trylock; may be recursive or not; implements critical section se

nodes.def: Two-thread mutual exclusion algorithm using shared flags and a turn variable; provides bounded waiting under sequential consistency but fails on modern weak-memory hardware without

nodes.label: relaxed memory model
nodes.def: Memory model that permits more reorderings than sequential consistency; allows loads to be reordered with respect to stores, stores to be reordered with respect to stores, etc. Exa

nodes.label: semaphore
nodes.def: Synchronization primitive maintaining a counter representing available permits; P (wait/decrement) and V (signal/increment) operations; can control N concurrent accesses to a resou

nodes.label: sequential consistency
nodes.def: Memory model where all operations appear to execute in some total order consistent with program order on each thread; the default intuitive model where every load reads the result

nodes.label: total store order tso
nodes.def: Memory model used by x86/x64 processors where stores are globally ordered but may be buffered locally before becoming visible to other cores; a stronger model than ARM/PowerPC that

nodes.label: aba problem
nodes.def: Race condition in CAS-based algorithms where value changes from A to B and back to A between check and update, fooling CAS into succeeding incorrectly; solved with tagged pointers

nodes.label: atomic exchange
nodes.def: Atomic operation that reads the current value of a variable and writes a new value in a single indivisible step, returning the old value.

nodes.label: backoff iteration
nodes.def: Zero-based counter tracking how many consecutive failed lock acquisition attempts have occurred since last success.

nodes.label: backoff multiplier
nodes.def: Scaling factor (commonly 2.0) that multiplies the current delay on each failed acquisition attempt to produce the next delay interval.

nodes.label: base delay
nodes.def: Initial wait time in nanoseconds or microseconds before the first lock acquisition retry; the starting point of the exponential schedule.

nodes.label: cache line ping pong
nodes.def: Performance anti-pattern where threads on different cores repeatedly invalidate each other's cache line, causing excessive coherency traffic; often caused by false sharing or poorl

nodes.label: data race
nodes.def: Specific concurrent access where at least one access is a write, accesses are to same memory location, and accesses are not properly synchronized; undefined behavior in C11/C++11.

nodes.label: delay ceiling
nodes.def: Upper bound cap on the computed delay; prevents unbounded growth of wait times when contention persists across many iterations.

nodes.label: dining philosophers
nodes.def: Classic deadlock problem with N philosophers at circular table needing both adjacent forks; demonstrates resource ordering, deadlock avoidance, and starvation-free synchronization

nodes.label: hazard pointers
nodes.def: Memory reclamation technique where each thread publishes dangerous pointers to globally accessible locations; memory cannot be reclaimed while referenced by any hazard pointer.

nodes.label: lamport bakery algorithm
nodes.def: N-thread mutual exclusion algorithm providing first-come-first-served ordering; uses ticket numbers; correct under sequential consistency but requires adaptation for weak memory mo

nodes.label: mcs lock acquire
nodes.def: Operation by which a thread obtains the lock; spins polling its own qnode.locked field until false; returns only after predecessor has released and cleared the flag; no shared atom

nodes.label: mcs lock wait for successor
nodes.def: Sub-protocol when release finds no successor yet linked; thread performing release or a helper spins on qnode.next until non-null; ensures no lock holder exits before its successor

nodes.label: memory fence
nodes.def: Synonym for memory barrier; hardware instruction enforcing visibility and ordering constraints on memory operations across the fence; variations include full fence, store fence, lo

nodes.label: memory order acquire
nodes.def: Memory ordering barrier ensuring all loads and stores after the barrier in program order cannot be reordered before it, synchronizing with release stores.

nodes.label: mesi protocol
nodes.def: Four-state cache coherency protocol: Modified (exclusive, dirty), Exclusive (exclusive, clean), Shared (shared, clean), Invalid (not present); prevents inconsistent cached data.

nodes.label: monitor
nodes.def: High-level synchronization construct combining mutex and condition variables; object-oriented abstraction where methods acquire lock automatically; ensures serialized access to obj

nodes.label: out of order execution
nodes.def: CPU feature executing instructions in data-dependency order rather than program order; enables utilization of unused execution units; interacts with memory ordering guarantees.

nodes.label: priority inversion
nodes.def: Problem where low-priority thread blocks high-priority thread by holding a lock needed by both; typically resolved via priority inheritance protocols.

nodes.label: reader writer lock
nodes.def: Synchronization primitive allowing multiple concurrent readers or exclusive single writer; improves read-heavy workloads but has higher overhead than simple mutex.

nodes.label: readers writers problem
nodes.def: Synchronization problem requiring exclusive write access but concurrent read access; solutions vary in reader/writer preference, fairness, and implementation complexity.

nodes.label: relaxed atomicity guarantee
nodes.def: The sole guarantee provided by memory_order_relaxed: the atomic variable is read and written atomically without tearing, but no ordering constraints are imposed on other operations

nodes.label: reordering freedom privilege
nodes.def: A relaxed atomic operation imposes no constraints on the reordering of memory operations by either the compiler or the hardware; the operation may be reordered with any other opera

nodes.label: seq cst global total order
nodes.def: A single total order of all sequentially consistent operations that is visible and agreed upon by all threads in the system; the interleaving point where all threads observe the sa

nodes.label: seq cst synchronization protocol
nodes.def: The protocol by which sequentially consistent operations establish synchronization points between threads; creates a happens-before relationship across thread boundaries.

nodes.label: software transactional memory stm
nodes.def: Transactional memory implemented entirely in software; threads validate read sets and write sets; higher overhead than HTM but works on any hardware; examples: TL2, DSTM.

nodes.label: store buffering
nodes.def: Phenomenon where a store may be buffered and become visible later, allowing a subsequent load to observe a stale value while other threads see different orderings.

nodes.label: synchronizes with absence
nodes.def: A relaxed atomic operation does not synchronize with any other operation; it establishes no happens-before or synchronizes-with relationship with any thread, including the thread t

nodes.label: transactional memory
nodes.def: Concurrency control paradigm allowing sequences of operations to execute atomically without explicit locking; either hardware-assisted (HTM), software-only (STM), or hybrid.

nodes.label: amdahl law
nodes.def: Formula limiting parallel speedup by the serial fraction of computation; speedup <= 1 / (serial_fraction + parallel_fraction / num_threads); motivates minimization of synchronized

nodes.label: arm memory model
nodes.def: Weak memory model used by ARM processors where memory operations may be reordered extensively unless explicitly ordered by barriers; most permissive of common architectures.

nodes.label: atomic compare exchange
nodes.def: C++11/C11 atomic operation attempting to replace expected value with desired; returns boolean indicating success; on failure, expected is updated with actual value for retry loops.

nodes.label: binary semaphore
nodes.def: Semaphore with counter restricted to 0 or 1; functions like a mutex but without ownership semantics; can be signaled by non-owner thread.

nodes.label: bounded waiting
nodes.def: Property requiring that after a thread requests entry to a critical section, there is a bound on the number of other threads allowed to enter before the requester.

nodes.label: cache alignment
nodes.def: Placement of data structures on memory boundaries matching cache line size, typically 64 bytes, preventing false sharing between adjacent data.

nodes.label: causal consistency boundary
nodes.def: Relaxed operations respect intra-thread causality (program order) but do not guarantee inter-thread causality; this boundary defines the scope of what relaxed_atomicity guarantees.

nodes.label: channel csp
nodes.def: Communication primitive from Communicating Sequential Processes model; send and receive operations synchronize producers and consumers; implementations include Go channels, Clojure

nodes.label: clh lock
nodes.def: Queued lock using a linked list of nodes with spinning on predecessor's flag; provides scalability and fairness similar to MCS but different cache behavior.

nodes.label: coherence

nodes.label: compiler barrier
nodes.def: Directive preventing the compiler from reordering memory operations across the barrier; does not emit hardware instructions but prevents compiler optimization from causing races.

nodes.label: completable future
nodes.def: Java class implementing Future with completion callbacks, chaining, and composition; supports thenApply, thenCompose, exceptionally; enables non-blocking asynchronous pipelines.

nodes.label: condition variable
nodes.def: Primitive enabling a thread to wait for a condition to become true; must be used with a mutex; wait atomically releases the mutex and blocks; notify/notify_all wake waiting threads

nodes.label: context switch
nodes.def: Operating system operation saving one thread's state and restoring another's; involves kernel transition, register saves, TLB invalidation; cost motivates lock-free and per-thread

nodes.label: countdown latch
nodes.def: One-time barrier initialized with a count; threads decrement count on completion; barrier opens when count reaches zero; cannot be reused.

nodes.label: counting semaphore
nodes.def: General semaphore with non-negative integer counter allowing multiple concurrent accesses; used for resource pooling and bounded work distribution.

nodes.label: cpp11 memory model
nodes.def: C++11 and later standard library memory model supporting atomic operations with configurable ordering; provides std::atomic with memory_order enum values matching C11 semantics.

nodes.label: cross thread visibility non global
nodes.def: Other threads may observe relaxed operations in any order relative to each other; there is no single total order visible to all threads as there is with sequentially_consistent.

nodes.label: cyclic barrier
nodes.def: Barrier implementation that resets after all threads pass; supports configurable thread count and optional action executed when barrier breaks.

nodes.label: deadlock prevention
nodes.def: Design strategies eliminating one of the four Coffman conditions: no circular wait (lock ordering), hold-and-wait (acquire all at once), preemption (non-preemptive resources), mutu

nodes.label: decorrelated jitter
nodes.def: Jitter strategy where each thread computes delay = random.uniform(min_delay, previous_delay * 3); history-dependent decorrelation reduces coordinated retry waves.

nodes.label: dekker algorithm
nodes.def: First correct two-process mutual exclusion algorithm achieving progress under sequential consistency; combines turn-taking with turn variable; also fails under relaxed memory order

nodes.label: epoch based reclamation
nodes.def: Memory reclamation scheme batching deletions into epochs; threads must wait for active epochs to complete before reclaiming protected memory; balances throughput and safety.

nodes.label: equal jitter
nodes.def: Jitter strategy computing delay = base_delay / 2 + random.uniform(0, base_delay / 2); ensures wait never falls below half the nominal delay.

nodes.label: false sharing
nodes.def: Performance problem where unrelated variables sharing a cache line cause cache coherency traffic when one is modified; threads updating different variables contend due to line-leve

nodes.label: fetch and add
nodes.def: Atomic operation returning old value while atomically incrementing memory location; used for counters, ticket distribution, and implementing certain lock-free structures.

nodes.label: full jitter
nodes.def: Jitter strategy selecting a uniform random value in the range [0, current_delay]; maximizes desynchronization at the cost of potentially very short waits.

nodes.label: futex
nodes.def: Fast userspace mutex kernel-assisted synchronization; userspace spinning first, then syscall to kernel for wait/wake; basis for most Linux threading primitives.

nodes.label: future promise
nodes.def: Concurrency pattern decoupling value computation from access; Future represents pending result, Promise provides completion mechanism; enables asynchronous composition.

nodes.label: instruction reordering
nodes.def: CPU or compiler reordering of memory operations for performance while preserving single-thread correctness; can violate programmer expectations in concurrent code without proper ba

nodes.label: intra thread program order
nodes.def: Within a single thread, the thread still observes its own relaxed operations in program order; this total order is local to the thread and not shared.

nodes.label: invalidate queue
nodes.def: Hardware queue holding pending invalidation requests for cache lines; entries must be drained before a core can ensure it has exclusive ownership of a cache line.

nodes.label: linearizability
nodes.def: Correctness criterion requiring each operation appear to execute atomically at some point between invocation and response; composable property essential for concurrent object speci

nodes.label: livelock
nodes.def: Failure where threads continuously respond to each other without making progress; distinguishable from deadlock by active state; often result of excessive collision avoidance.

nodes.label: load buffering
nodes.def: Phenomenon in weak memory models where a load may observe a store from a different thread that happens later in global order, enabling patterns impossible under SC.

nodes.label: load linked store conditional
nodes.def: Pair of instructions for software atomic operations: LL reads atomically, SC writes only if no intervening store occurred; used on ARM, PowerPC; avoids ABA problem inherent to CAS.

nodes.label: lock elision

nodes.label: mcs lock fifo ordering
nodes.def: Property guaranteed by MCS queue structure; lock acquisition order matches the order of enqueue operations; provides fairness without centralized ticket counters.

nodes.label: mcs lock help links
nodes.def: Backoff resolution protocol during failed enqueue CAS; the thread that lost the CAS follows the discovered pointer chain to complete the linking work of the winner before retrying

nodes.label: mcs lock local spinning
nodes.def: Performance property of MCS; each waiter spins on its own thread-local qnode in its own cache line; eliminates cache-line ping-ponging between spinning threads; reduces bus traffic

nodes.label: mcs lock qnode locked
nodes.def: Boolean field in qnode; spinning thread reads this; set true on enqueue and cleared false by predecessor upon release; default true indicates lock not yet released.

nodes.label: mcs lock qnode next
nodes.def: Pointer field in qnode referencing successor qnode; null until predecessor links this node; spinning thread polls this to detect when it has been chained into the queue.

nodes.label: mcs lock tail
nodes.def: Atomic shared pointer to the last enqueued qnode; initialized null; updated via CAS during enqueue; represents the lock acquisition frontier.

nodes.def: C11/C++11 memory ordering that only guarantees atomicity of the operation with no ordering constraints relative to other operations; allows all reorderings.

nodes.label: memory order release
nodes.def: Memory ordering barrier ensuring all loads and stores before the barrier in program order cannot be reordered after it, making prior writes visible to acquiring threads.

nodes.label: mutex livelock prevention
nodes.def: Techniques including exponential backoff, random delays, or lock registry to prevent threads from repeatedly colliding on lock acquisition.

nodes.label: no happens before establishment
nodes.def: A relaxed operation neither participates in nor establishes a happens-before relationship with any other operation; operations may be reordered arbitrarily across thread boundaries

nodes.label: no synchronizes with establishment
nodes.def: A relaxed operation cannot synchronize-with any operation on another thread; release semantics and acquire semantics are absent, breaking the synchronizes-with chain.

nodes.label: numa awareness
nodes.def: Design consideration for systems with non-uniform memory access latency; thread affinity and data placement affect performance; synchronization must account for remote vs local mem

nodes.label: obstruction free
nodes.def: Progress guarantee where a thread completes an operation if it runs alone without interference; may starve under contention but has no blocking operations.

nodes.label: powerpc memory model
nodes.def: Weak memory model used by PowerPC/POWER processors with similar permissiveness to ARM; requires explicit barriers for many ordering guarantees.

nodes.label: priority inheritance
nodes.def: Protocol resolving priority inversion by temporarily elevating the priority of a lock-holding low-priority thread to match the highest blocked thread.

nodes.label: producer consumer
nodes.def: Concurrent pattern with producer threads generating work consumed by consumer threads; typically synchronized with bounded or unbounded channels/queues.

nodes.label: atomicity
nodes.def: The all-or-nothing property: a transaction's effects are either fully applied or fully absent; implemented via undo_log and transaction rollback.

nodes.label: isolation level
nodes.def: A configurable parameter defining the degree to which concurrent transactions are isolated from each other's uncommitted or intermediate effects.

nodes.label: rollback
nodes.def: The act of undoing a transaction's effects using undo_log entries, returning the database to its pre-transaction state.

nodes.label: tl log record
nodes.def: The fundamental unit of a transaction_log: a single append-only entry recording one atomic change or lifecycle event made by a transaction; identified by an lsn.

nodes.label: read committed
nodes.def: An isolation_level where each statement sees only data committed before that statement begins; prevents dirty_read but allows non_repeatable_read and phantom_read.

nodes.label: row level locking
nodes.def: Lock management at the individual row granularity via row_lock entries in lock_manager's lock table; enables high concurrency but increases lock_manager overhead.

nodes.label: transaction state
nodes.def: The current phase of a transaction lifecycle: active, partially_committed, committed, aborted; drives lock release and recovery behavior.

nodes.label: acid properties
nodes.def: The four guarantees of database transactions: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability — the foundational contract between a DBMS and its clients.

nodes.label: commit
nodes.def: The act of making a transaction's effects permanent: flush log records to durable storage, release locks, transition transaction_state to committed.

nodes.label: concurrency control
nodes.def: The set of mechanisms a DBMS uses to manage simultaneous access to shared data while preserving correctness and isolation guarantees.

nodes.label: database transaction
nodes.def: A logical unit of work executed against a database, bounded by BEGIN and COMMIT/ROLLBACK, guaranteeing ACID properties across one or more SQL operations.

nodes.label: dirty read
nodes.def: An anomaly where a transaction reads data written by another transaction that has not yet committed; only possible in read_uncommitted.

nodes.label: commit visibility boundary
nodes.def: temporal threshold in read_committed: a datum is visible iff its committing_transaction committed before the reading statement started

nodes.label: committed data
nodes.def: database state resulting from successfully completed transactions; constitutes the visible universe for read_committed queries

nodes.label: exclusive lock
nodes.def: A lock type granting sole read-write access to a resource; incompatible with all other lock types including shared_lock and update_lock.

nodes.label: undo log
nodes.def: Log records describing the previous state of modified data; used to undo uncommitted transaction changes during rollback and recovery.

nodes.label: write ahead logging
nodes.def: A protocol requiring log records be flushed to durable storage before the corresponding data changes are applied; ensures durability and atomicity.

nodes.label: write lock held until commit
nodes.def: exclusive lock discipline in read_committed requiring a transaction to hold write locks on modified rows until transaction commit or rollback

nodes.label: before image
nodes.def: The committed database state of a row immediately before a transaction modifies it; recorded in the undo_log so the modification can be undone if the transaction rolls back.

nodes.label: committed
nodes.def: The terminal transaction_state after durable persistence of all changes; locks are released per locking_protocol rules.

nodes.label: lock granularity
nodes.def: The size of the database object protected by a lock: row_lock, page_lock, table_lock — trading off concurrency against lock_manager overhead.

nodes.label: read uncommitted
nodes.def: The weakest isolation_level: transactions may observe uncommitted changes from other transactions, permitting dirty_read.

nodes.label: statement
nodes.def: A single SQL operation within a transaction; atomicity requires that each statement either fully completes its effect or fully reverts before the next statement begins.

nodes.label: statement level read consistency
nodes.def: guarantee within read_committed that each SQL statement sees all changes committed at the moment that statement began execution

nodes.label: tl checkpoint record
nodes.def: A special log_record written periodically by a checkpoint_writer; records the volatile database state at a consistent point, bounding the recovery_manager's replay horizon.

nodes.label: tl undo log
nodes.def: A structured collection of tl_update_record entries chained by a transaction; traversed in reverse order during rollback to restore the before_image of each modified entity.

nodes.label: tl update record
nodes.def: A log_record capturing a before_image and after_image of a modified data page or row; used by both redo_recovery (for durability) and undo_recovery (for atomicity rollback).

nodes.label: transaction boundary

nodes.label: transaction log
nodes.def: An append-only sequence of records tracking every change made by transactions; the primary mechanism for atomicity and durability.

nodes.label: two phase locking
nodes.def: A locking_protocol where transactions must acquire all locks during a growing_phase and release all locks during a shrinking_phase, guaranteeing conflict_serializable schedules.

nodes.label: uncommitted change
nodes.def: A modification to database state made by a transaction that has not yet committed; visible to other transactions at read_uncommitted.

nodes.label: aborted state
nodes.def: The terminal transaction_state after rollback completes; all acquired locks are released and the transaction cannot be restarted automatically.

nodes.label: all or nothing
nodes.def: The conceptual guarantee that a transaction executes as an indivisible unit: either every operation succeeds or no operation has any effect.

nodes.label: consistency
nodes.def: A transaction transforms the database from one valid state to another, preserving all defined integrity constraints and business rules.

nodes.label: isolation
nodes.def: The property that concurrently executing transactions do not interfere with each other; the degree of interference is controlled by isolation_level.

nodes.label: lock timeout handling
nodes.def: timeout mechanism in read_committed for transactions blocked waiting to acquire conflicting locks on rows

nodes.label: locking protocol
nodes.def: A disciplined set of rules governing when locks may be acquired and released to ensure serializability or other isolation guarantees.

nodes.label: non repeatable read possible
nodes.def: the permitted anomaly in read_committed: a transaction reading the same row twice may observe different values if a concurrent transaction updates and commits that row between read

nodes.label: optimistic cc
nodes.def: Concurrency control strategy that permits unrestricted execution and detects conflicts only at validation_phase, aborting and retrying on conflict.

nodes.label: serializable
nodes.def: The strongest isolation_level: the result of executing concurrent transactions is equivalent to some serial order of those transactions; prevents all anomalies.

nodes.label: statement start timestamp

nodes.label: strict two phase locking
nodes.def: A variant of two_phase_locking where exclusive_locks are held until transaction end, ensuring strict_schedule and enabling cascading_less schedules.

nodes.label: timestamp ordering
nodes.def: A concurrency control method assigning timestamps to transactions and using them to order operations, ensuring serializability without locking.

nodes.label: tl abort record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction enters the aborted_state; signals that undo_log entries must be applied to reverse this transaction's effects.

nodes.label: tl checkpoint writer
nodes.def: The subsystem component that periodically writes a tl_checkpoint_record to the transaction_log; trims obsolete log segments and bounds crash_recovery time.

nodes.label: tl commit record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction commits; marks the durable persistence boundary for durability guarantees; flushed to disk before the transaction releases its locks.

nodes.def: A runtime data structure maintained by recovery_manager listing data pages modified but not yet flushed; consulted during checkpoint to ensure write_ahead_logging invariants hold.

nodes.label: transaction read
nodes.def: The act of a transaction executing a read operation; at read_uncommitted this read may return uncommitted_change from concurrent transactions.

nodes.label: update lock
nodes.def: A lock type that prevents deadlock during lock_upgrade: compatible with shared_lock but not with other update_locks or exclusive_locks.

nodes.label: write lock not required
nodes.def: The characteristic of read_uncommitted where a writing transaction does not hold an exclusive lock preventing other transactions from reading its uncommitted state.

nodes.label: active state

nodes.def: Configured program git attributes runs on git checkout; transforms blob from object store before writing to working tree.

nodes.label: commit graph write
nodes.def: git commit-graph write traverses reachable commits and writes binary graph; --split merges small chains; --append adds commits to existing graph.

nodes.label: commit message encoding message bytes
nodes.def: Raw byte sequence forming the commit message body; decoded using encoding_value (or assumed UTF-8) to produce display characters.

nodes.label: commit message encoding transcoded message
nodes.def: The output of transcoding_logic: message_bytes decoded then re-encoded into log_encoding_flag; git log emits this to the terminal.

nodes.label: committer field
nodes.def: Name, email, timestamp, and timezone offset in commit object; records who committed (not necessarily who authored).

nodes.label: custom object db
nodes.def: Alternative backend via GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY or extensions.objectFormat; allows SHA-256, shared storage, or plugin-based stores.

nodes.label: executable file mode
nodes.def: Mode 100755; regular file with execute bits set; Git marks it this way to preserve the executable bit across platforms that handle it differently.

nodes.label: fetch head
nodes.def: Temporary .git/FETCH_HEAD file recording all branches fetched and their merge configuration for the next pull operation.

nodes.label: fsck integrity
nodes.def: git fsck traverses all reachable objects validating SHA-1 linkage, ref integrity, and accessibility; reports dangling and unreachable.

nodes.label: gc prune
nodes.def: Garbage collection process expunging unreachable objects older than prune.window; configurable via gc.prune expire and git prune.

nodes.label: graft point
nodes.def: File .git/info/grafts (or .git/shallow) overriding or truncating commit ancestry; used for repository imports with incomplete history.

nodes.label: hash object write
nodes.def: Flag hash --write causes git to store the computed object in .git/objects/ after hashing; idempotent on repeat.

nodes.label: heads namespace
nodes.def: Namespace .git/refs/heads/ containing local branch references; each file = branch name; its SHA-1 = tip commit.

nodes.label: mode bit format
nodes.def: Base-8 positional numeral system used to encode file mode; Git stores exactly 6 octal digits representing 18 bits of mode information.

nodes.label: octopus merge
nodes.def: Merge commit with more than two parents; octopus strategy combines multiple branches; refs/heads/main lists all parents in merge commit object.

nodes.label: packed refs
nodes.def: Consolidated .git/packed-refs file containing refs not in loose format; created by git pack-refs; enables faster startup on repos with many refs.

nodes.label: packfile bitmap
nodes.def: Reachability bitmap at packfile end enabling fast network transfer negotiation and clone/fetch optimization by marking all reachable objects.

nodes.label: packfile negotiation
nodes.def: Smart protocol phase where server advertises reachable refs and client computes minimum packfile of missing objects using haves/wants.

nodes.label: rebase replay
nodes.def: Replay commits as new objects onto new base; each original commit replaced; original SHA-1s abandoned; creates new history branch.

nodes.label: refspec
nodes.def: Pattern mapping source to destination ref during fetch/push: [+]<src>:<dst>; enables selective branch transfer and namespace rewriting.

nodes.label: regular file mode
nodes.def: Mode 100644; standard blob-backed file with read permission for all and write for owner; the default for non-executable files committed to Git.

nodes.label: remotes namespace
nodes.def: Namespace .git/refs/remotes/ containing remote-tracking branches; updated by fetch, not by user edits; represent server state.

nodes.label: replace ref
nodes.def: Reference under refs/replace/ mapping an object SHA to a substitute SHA; transparent to most commands; allows history rewriting without modifying history.

nodes.label: sha1 collision resistance
nodes.def: Property that finding two distinct contents with same SHA-1 requires ~2^80 operations; git relies on this for object identity.

nodes.label: sha256 migration
nodes.def: Gradual transition from SHA-1 to SHA-256 object names; support for SHA-256-only repositories since git 2.29; object format stored in config.

nodes.label: shallow clone
nodes.def: Clone with .git/shallow cut-off file listing shallow commit SHAs; prevents fetching ancestors beyond the boundary.

nodes.label: smudge filter
nodes.def: Configured program git attributes runs on git add; transforms working-tree file before storing as object; lazy loading via .gitattributes.

nodes.label: stash ref
nodes.def: Pseudo-branch at refs/stash maintained by git stash; each stash entry is a commit whose tree captures working-directory state.

nodes.label: subtree mode
nodes.def: Mode 040000; entry points to a nested tree object representing a directory; the tree entry name contains a forward slash but the slash is not stored in the entry itself.

nodes.label: symlink mode
nodes.def: Mode 120000; entry points to a blob object containing the target path as raw bytes; the blob content is the symlink destination, not the link data itself.

nodes.label: tree entry name
nodes.def: Null-terminated byte string within tree entry; may contain slash for subdirectory entries; case-sensitive on all platforms.

nodes.label: worktree pointer
nodes.def: File .git/worktrees/<name>/HEAD and GITDIR files linking a linked working tree to the main repository's object store and refs.

nodes.label: zlib compression
nodes.def: Deflate compression applied to all loose object content and packfile entries; balance of speed and ratio; configurable per object type via core.compression.

nodes.label: annotated tag signature
nodes.def: PGP signature stored within tag object body; verified by git tag -v; authenticates the tagged object SHA-1.

nodes.label: author email
nodes.def: String component of the author field in a commit object specifying the primary creator's email address; appears in angle brackets after the name in the standard <name> <email> form

nodes.label: author ident
nodes.def: Full author identity string in the form 'Name <email> timestamp timezone_offset' embedded in a commit object's author header; the canonical representation of author_field.

nodes.label: author identification
nodes.def: The combination of author_name and author_email forming the author's identity within the commit object.

nodes.label: author rfc2822
nodes.def: The RFC 2822 formatted author line: "author <name> <email> <timestamp> <timezone>" stored in commit object body.

nodes.label: author timezone
nodes.def: String timezone offset in the author field following the timestamp; formatted as +HHMM or -HHMM indicating hours and minutes east or west of UTC.

nodes.label: author vs committer
nodes.def: The semantic distinction: author created the patch content; committer applied it to the repository; git blame uses author_field as the primary attribution.

nodes.label: bisect log
nodes.def: refs/bisect/* pseudo-refs tracking midpoints and test results during git bisect; --no-checkout mode walks history without checkout.

nodes.label: blob prefetch
nodes.def: Git fetch-object or protocol v2 advertisements retrieving missing blob content on demand from partial clone; requires server support.

nodes.label: blob split threshold
nodes.def: Configuration core.bigFileThreshold beyond which git may store deltas instead of full content in packfiles.

nodes.label: bloom filter index
nodes.def: Commit-graph embedded data structure encoding paths modified per commit; powers git log --S <string> --throughput optimization.

nodes.label: branch tracking assignment
nodes.def: Remote-tracking ref establishing upstream relationship; configured via branch.<name>.remote and branch.<name>.merge; used for push.default and @{upstream}.

nodes.label: byte string content
nodes.def: The raw byte sequence forming the name; git stores no encoding assumption, no null bytes permitted within the name itself, and no guaranteed UTF-8 validity.

nodes.label: case preservation property
nodes.def: The name bytes are stored verbatim and compared byte-for-byte, making the entry case-sensitive on all operating systems including case-insensitive filesystems where the working tre

nodes.label: cherry pick delta
nodes.def: Apply single commit's diff as new commit; preserves original author; generates new SHA-1; records original SHA-1 in commit message.

nodes.label: commit date ordering
nodes.def: Revision list ordering by commit timestamp; --date-order flag; faster than topological but produces non-ancestor-first sequences.

nodes.label: commit filter
nodes.def: Revision traversal predicate (--since, --author, --grep, --S, --G) restricting which commits appear in output.

nodes.label: commit graph verify
nodes.def: git commit-graph verify reads graph and validates generation numbers, checksum, and fanout structure; reports corruption.

nodes.label: commit message encoding
nodes.def: Commit object may record encoding header; git log --encoding=UTF-8 transcodes as needed; enables non-ASCII commit messages.

nodes.label: commit message encoding display encoding
nodes.def: The terminal or output stream encoding git uses when writing the transcoded_message; git assumes UTF-8 output if terminal encoding is unset.

nodes.label: commit message encoding encoding absence
nodes.def: State when a commit object lacks an encoding header; git treats the message as UTF-8 by default per the unicode interpretation rule.

nodes.label: commit message encoding encoding fallback
nodes.def: Fallback behavior when transcoding_logic cannot map a character; typically replaces with a substitution character or skips the byte.

nodes.label: commit message encoding log encoding flag
nodes.def: git log flag --encoding=<enc> specifying the target encoding for transcoded output; overrides the stored encoding for display purposes.

nodes.label: commit message encoding original encoding
nodes.def: Alias for encoding_value; the encoding recorded at commit time distinguishing the message's original byte interpretation from the display encoding.

nodes.label: committer ident
nodes.def: Full committer identity string in form 'Name <email> timestamp timezone_offset' in the commit object; distinct from author_ident.

nodes.label: compression level
nodes.def: Integer -1 (zlib default), 0 (store), 1-9 (fast to best); set via core.compression or per-object pack-objects --compression.

nodes.label: copy instruction
nodes.def: Packfile command copying bytes from base object at offset+length; encodes file copy without recompression.

nodes.label: crc32 checksum
nodes.def: Checksum stored per object in packfile index; verified on read to detect corruption before decompression.

nodes.label: dangling blob
nodes.def: Blob object with no parent tree entry; arises from aborted rebase or staged-but-uncommitted content; harmless but obscures analysis.

nodes.label: delta island
nodes.def: Packfile grouping mechanism isolating objects reachable via specific refs; prevents cross-island delta sharing; aids monorepo incremental fetch.

nodes.label: embedded null rejection
nodes.def: The rule that a tree entry name cannot contain an internal null byte because null is the field terminator; any such byte would truncate the name prematurely.

nodes.label: empty tree sha
nodes.def: SHA-1 of the empty tree (tree with zero entries): 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904; used as synthetic parent of root commits.

nodes.label: forward slash byte
nodes.def: The octet value 0x2F representing the ASCII forward slash character; signals subdirectory boundary in tree entry name byte sequences.

nodes.label: fsync object write
nodes.def: System call flushing object file to durable storage; controlled by core.fsyncObjectFiles; trades safety against write throughput.

nodes.label: generation number
nodes.def: Integer in commit-graph measuring topological distance from roots; enables fast ancestor queries without traversing full commit history.

nodes.label: graph tip
nodes.def: Commit referenced by a branch tip; all ancestors reachable; descendant commits unreferenced subject to gc if no other path retains them.

nodes.label: hook environment
nodes.def: Environment variables (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH) passed to hook executables; quarantine prevents bad objects from entering repo.

nodes.label: hook trigger
nodes.def: Executable script under .git/hooks/ invoked by specific git commands (pre-commit, post-commit, pre-rebase, etc.); nonzero exit aborts operation.

nodes.label: insert instruction
nodes.def: Packfile command appending literal byte sequence to output; the raw new content not derivable from base.

nodes.label: linear history heuristic
nodes.def: Git's default rebase behavior assumes first parent path is mainline; git log --first-parent exposes linearized view; bisect follows first parent.

nodes.label: loose object
nodes.def: Individual compressed file stored at .git/objects/xx/xxxx...; fast to write but inefficient at scale; one object per file.

nodes.label: maintenance scheduler
nodes.def: Background git maintenance --scheduled running via cron or systemd timer; config thresholds in maintenance.<task>.schedule.

nodes.label: mode permission bits
nodes.def: The lower 9 bits (three octal digits) encoding Unix owner/group/other read-write-execute permissions; displayed as the last three digits of the 6-digit octal mode.

nodes.label: mode zero padding
nodes.def: The leading zero in modes like 100644 and 040000 ensures consistent 6-digit width; the zero fills the third octal digit reserved for special file type flags.

nodes.label: multi pack index
nodes.def: Compound .midx file spanning multiple packfiles; enables cross-pack object queries and accelerates repack scenarios.

nodes.label: note object
nodes.def: Blob-like object linked via refs/notes/commits/ to commits; provides annotation layer outside normal commit history.

nodes.label: null termination semantics
nodes.def: The rule that a null byte (0x00) terminates the tree entry name field, separating it from the following mode and SHA-1 blob reference within the tree entry binary structure.

nodes.label: object header
nodes.def: Four-byte prefix of every loose object: type byte + space + decimal size + null byte before payload; enables streaming deserialization.

nodes.label: octopus strategy
nodes.def: Merge strategy handling 3+ branch tips simultaneously; creates single commit with all parents; avoids intermediate pairwise merges.

nodes.label: ofs delta
nodes.def: Delta format encoding base object as relative offset within packfile; safer for streaming than REF_DELTA which names base by SHA-1.

nodes.label: ours strategy
nodes.def: Merge strategy favoring current branch content for conflicts; creates new commit with all parents but discards theirs content.

nodes.label: path separator notation
nodes.def: The forward slash character (0x2F) embedded within the name byte string signals a directory boundary; git parses no actual directory structure, only the slash as a naming conventio

nodes.label: causal inference
nodes.def: reasoning about cause-effect relationships enabling prediction of consequences given observed causes

nodes.label: consistency
nodes.def: A reasoning task verifying that an ontology has no contradictory axioms that would eliminate all possible models.

nodes.label: counterfactual reasoning
nodes.def: reasoning about hypothetical alternative scenarios and their outcomes differing from actual observed events

nodes.label: tbox
nodes.def: The terminological box — the schema-level component of a knowledge base defining classes, properties, and their relations.

nodes.label: abox
nodes.def: The assertional box — the instance-level component of a knowledge base containing ground assertions about individuals.

nodes.label: annotation property
nodes.def: A property type for attaching metadata (labels, comments, deprecated flags) without affecting reasoning.

nodes.label: application ontology
nodes.def: A concrete ontology tailored for a specific software application, integrating and constraining reference and domain ontologies.

nodes.label: axiom
nodes.def: A logical statement in an ontology taken as fundamental truth, constraining what inferences and interpretations are valid.

nodes.label: backward chaining
nodes.def: An inference strategy starting from a query goal and recursively applying rules backwards to find supporting facts.

nodes.label: blank node
nodes.def: An anonymous resource in RDF without a stable IRI, used for existential variables or intermediate blank graph nodes.

nodes.label: cardinality restriction
nodes.def: A class restriction specifying exact, minimum, or maximum number of values a property can take for class members.

nodes.label: class
nodes.def: A concept in an ontology representing a set of entities that share common characteristics, forming the taxonomic backbone.

nodes.label: class assertion
nodes.def: statement asserting that an individual entity belongs to a specific class in the ontology classification system

nodes.label: classification
nodes.def: The process of organizing entities into classes based on shared characteristics, a core activity in ontology engineering.

nodes.label: coherence
nodes.def: The quality property of an ontology where all defined classes can have at least one instance without violating constraints.

nodes.label: concept hierarchy
nodes.def: organization of concepts in an ontology forming IS-A taxonomic relationships with superclass and subclass relations

nodes.label: concept similarity
nodes.def: metric quantifying the degree of semantic relatedness between two concepts based on shared attributes and relationships

nodes.label: confidence scoring
nodes.def: assignment of probability or confidence values to knowledge graph triples indicating reliability of each fact

nodes.label: constraint
nodes.def: A logical condition restricting valid states of a knowledge graph, violated instances indicating data quality issues.

nodes.label: constraint satisfaction
nodes.def: enforcement of logical rules and cardinality constraints ensuring knowledge graph consistency and validity

nodes.label: coreference
nodes.def: The relationship between different expressions referring to the same entity, central to entity resolution and data integration.

nodes.label: datatype property
nodes.def: A property type in OWL whose value is a literal datatype, attaching data values to entities.

nodes.label: domain ontology
nodes.def: An ontology capturing the concepts and relations specific to a particular subject area or application domain.

nodes.label: entity linking
nodes.def: process of connecting textual entity mentions to their corresponding nodes in a knowledge graph disambiguating meaning

nodes.label: evidence aggregation
nodes.def: process of combining evidence from multiple sources to determine the overall confidence in a knowledge assertion

nodes.label: forward chaining
nodes.def: An inference strategy applying rules repeatedly from premises to conclusions until no new facts can be derived.

nodes.label: graph pattern
nodes.def: A template of triple patterns with variables used in SPARQL queries to match and extract subgraphs from knowledge graphs.

nodes.label: named individual
nodes.def: An individual entity that is explicitly named with an IRI, as distinguished from anonymous blank nodes.

nodes.label: property assertion
nodes.def: triple asserting a specific relationship between two individuals or an individual and a literal value

nodes.label: qualified cardinality
nodes.def: A cardinality restriction in OWL 2 specifying the exact number of values from a specified class for a given property.

nodes.label: realization
nodes.def: The automated reasoning task of determining the most specific classes that apply to each individual in a knowledge base.

nodes.label: satisfiability
nodes.def: A reasoning task determining whether an ontology or class description can have any valid model satisfying all axioms.

nodes.label: semantic relation
nodes.def: An abstract typed connection between concepts or entities capturing meaningful domain-relevant associations.

nodes.label: subclass of
nodes.def: A taxonomic relation stating that one class is more specific than (a specialization of) another class.

nodes.label: taxonomy
nodes.def: A hierarchical classification structure organizing concepts from general to specific through subclass/superclass relationships.

nodes.label: validation
nodes.def: The checking of a knowledge graph against defined constraints to identify violations indicating errors or inconsistencies.

nodes.label: abductive reasoning
nodes.def: inference process that derives the most likely explanation for observed facts given available knowledge

nodes.label: description logic
nodes.def: The decidable fragment of first-order logic underpinning OWL, balancing expressive power with tractable reasoning.

nodes.label: disjoint class
nodes.def: ontology axiom ensuring instances of one class cannot simultaneously belong to another specified class

nodes.label: disjoint union
nodes.def: A logical axiom stating that a class is exactly the union of a collection of pairwise-disjoint classes.

nodes.label: disjoint with
nodes.def: A logical constraint stating that two classes have no common instances, enforcing mutual exclusivity in domain models.

nodes.label: distant supervision
nodes.def: weak supervision technique using knowledge graph to generate training labels for relation extraction from text

nodes.label: dl safe rule
nodes.def: A rule in OWL 2 RL/RDF that is restricted to ensure decidability and compatibility with description logic semantics.

nodes.label: domain
nodes.def: The constraint specifying which classes an entity must belong to when it appears as the subject of a given property.

nodes.label: domain range
nodes.def: constraints defining which entity types can appear as subject or object of a given property in an ontology

nodes.label: entailment
nodes.def: A logical consequence relationship where one set of statements necessarily follows from another set given the formal semantics.

nodes.label: entity
nodes.def: A real or abstract thing represented as a node in a knowledge graph, identified by a unique IRI and having properties and relationships.

nodes.label: entity disambiguation
nodes.def: process of determining which specific real-world entity a text mention refers to when multiple candidates exist

nodes.label: entity representation learning
nodes.def: learning continuous vector embeddings for entities capturing their semantic properties and graph neighborhood

nodes.label: entity resolution
nodes.def: The task of identifying when multiple entity identifiers refer to the same real-world object, also called deduplication.

nodes.label: entity typing
nodes.def: task of assigning semantic types and classes to entities determining what categories they belong to in the ontology

nodes.label: equivalent class
nodes.def: A logical axiom declaring two class expressions to denote the same set of entities in an ontology.

nodes.label: equivalent property
nodes.def: A logical axiom declaring two properties to have identical semantics and extensions in an ontology.

nodes.label: existential restriction
nodes.def: A class restriction requiring that instances have at least one value for a specified property from a specified class.

nodes.label: fact checking
nodes.def: task of verifying the truthfulness of factual claims using knowledge graphs as a source of verified knowledge

nodes.label: formal ontology
nodes.def: An explicit specification of a conceptualization using a formal logic, enabling computational reasoning about domain structure.

nodes.label: foundational ontology
nodes.def: A top-level ontology supplying core metaphysical categories and relations for building domain ontologies on top of.

nodes.label: functional property
nodes.def: A property axiom stating that each entity can have at most one distinct value for this property.

nodes.label: graph
nodes.def: An abstract mathematical structure composed of nodes (vertices) and edges (connections) underlying all knowledge graph representations.

nodes.label: graph database
nodes.def: database management system optimized for graph storage and traversal operations enabling efficient knowledge graph queries

nodes.label: graph embedding
nodes.def: A learned low-dimensional vector representation of graph elements preserving structural and semantic proximity information.

nodes.label: graph neural network
nodes.def: A neural architecture designed to operate directly on graph-structured data, learning representations for nodes and edges.

nodes.label: graph query language
nodes.def: language designed for expressing pattern matching and traversal operations over graph-structured knowledge

nodes.label: graph traversal
nodes.def: The algorithmic process of visiting nodes and edges in a knowledge graph following defined patterns or strategies.

nodes.label: hierarchy
nodes.def: A parent-child tree structure imposing ordering among entities, fundamental to class taxonomies and part-whole relations.

nodes.label: hybrid reasoning
nodes.def: A reasoning approach combining multiple inference techniques such as description logic reasoning with rule-based logic programming.

nodes.label: indexing
nodes.def: The creation of auxiliary data structures enabling fast retrieval of triples matching given patterns in a triple store.

nodes.label: individual
nodes.def: A concrete instance of a class in an ontology, representing a specific entity in the domain rather than a type.

nodes.label: inductive learning
nodes.def: A learning setting where the model generalizes to entirely unseen entities not present during training.

nodes.label: inference
nodes.def: The process of deriving new implicit knowledge from explicit statements using logical rules and reasoning mechanisms.

nodes.label: inference engine
nodes.def: reasoning system that derives new implicit knowledge from explicit facts using logical rules and ontology constraints

nodes.label: instance of
nodes.def: A membership relation connecting an individual entity to the class it belongs to.

nodes.label: inverse functional property
nodes.def: A property axiom stating that the inverse of a property is functional, enabling inference of identity from property values.

nodes.label: inverse property
nodes.def: A logical axiom declaring that two properties are the mutual converse of each other in a relationship pair.

nodes.label: iri
nodes.def: Internationalized Resource Identifier — the global identifier standard for resources in the semantic web, replacing the older URI spec.

nodes.label: irreflexive property
nodes.def: A property axiom stating that no entity can relate to itself via the specified property.

nodes.label: json ld
nodes.def: JSON for Linked Data — a JSON-based serialization for RDF designed for ease of use by web developers.

nodes.label: knowledge base
nodes.def: A persistent storage system for structured knowledge, combining a knowledge graph with an inference engine and query interface.

nodes.label: knowledge completion inference
nodes.def: specialized inference focused on predicting missing facts by reasoning over existing knowledge graph structure

nodes.label: knowledge curation
nodes.def: ongoing process of reviewing validating updating and correcting knowledge stored in the graph

nodes.label: knowledge embedding
nodes.def: A vector representation of entities and relations in a knowledge graph learned to satisfy relational constraints geometrically.

nodes.label: knowledge graph
nodes.def: A structured representation of knowledge as a graph of entities (nodes) and their relationships (edges), enabling semantic querying and inference over interconnected data.

nodes.label: knowledge graph augmentation
nodes.def: process of enhancing an existing knowledge graph with additional facts entities or relations from external sources

nodes.label: knowledge graph completion
nodes.def: The task of automatically inferring missing facts in a knowledge graph to improve its coverage and utility.

nodes.label: knowledge graph construction
nodes.def: end-to-end process of building a knowledge graph from raw data sources including extraction integration and curation

nodes.label: knowledge graph embedding
nodes.def: specific embedding technique that projects knowledge graph components into continuous vector representations

nodes.label: knowledge graph fusion
nodes.def: process of merging multiple knowledge graphs into a unified graph resolving conflicts and eliminating duplicates

nodes.label: knowledge graph indexing
nodes.def: creation of efficient data structures enabling fast lookup and retrieval of entities and relations in the graph

nodes.label: knowledge graph linking
nodes.def: establishment of cross-references between entities in different knowledge graphs forming a linked knowledge network

nodes.label: knowledge graph query optimization
nodes.def: techniques for efficiently executing complex queries over large-scale knowledge graphs using indexing and planning

nodes.label: knowledge graph revision
nodes.def: process of modifying the knowledge graph to correct errors incorporate new information or adapt to changing knowledge

nodes.label: knowledge graph schema learning
nodes.def: automatic discovery of structural patterns and typing schemas from entity relationships in the graph

nodes.label: knowledge graph storage
nodes.def: physical organization of knowledge graph data in storage systems including indexing partitioning and caching strategies

nodes.label: knowledge ontology matching
nodes.def: process of aligning entities and relations between a knowledge graph and an external ontology reference schema

nodes.label: knowledge representation
nodes.def: The field of study concerned with how to formally encode knowledge so that computer systems can reason about it.

nodes.label: link neighbor
nodes.def: An entity adjacent to a given entity via one or more edges in a knowledge graph, forming the local neighborhood context.

nodes.label: link prediction
nodes.def: The task of inferring missing or likely future relationships between entities in a knowledge graph.

nodes.label: linked data
nodes.def: A set of best practices for publishing and interlinking structured data on the web using RDF and HTTP IRIs.

nodes.label: literal
nodes.def: A raw data value (string, number, date) in an RDF triple, as opposed to a reference to another entity via IRI.

nodes.label: literal value
nodes.def: data value like string number date or boolean attached to entities as property objects in knowledge representation

nodes.label: materialization
nodes.def: The pre-computation and storage of all inferred facts derivable from explicit knowledge, trading space for query speed.

nodes.label: module extraction
nodes.def: The extraction of a minimal relevant subset of an ontology satisfying all axioms relevant to a given signature of interest.

nodes.label: multi hop reasoning
nodes.def: The ability to traverse and compose multiple relational steps in a knowledge graph to derive complex inferred conclusions.

nodes.label: n triples
nodes.def: A line-oriented RDF serialization format where each triple appears on a single line as subject predicate object separated by spaces.

nodes.label: named entity recognition
nodes.def: NLP task of locating and classifying named entities in text into predefined categories like person organization location

nodes.label: named graph
nodes.def: An RDF graph identified by an IRI, enabling provenance tracking, access control, and multi-context knowledge representation.

nodes.label: namespace
nodes.def: A logical grouping of related identifiers under a common prefix, disambiguating terms and providing context for schema definitions.

nodes.label: neural symbolic
nodes.def: An approach integrating neural network learning with symbolic reasoning for enhanced knowledge graph completion and inference.

nodes.label: object
nodes.def: The third element of an RDF triple — the value or entity that is the target of the predicate assertion.

nodes.label: object property
nodes.def: A property type in OWL whose value is another individual entity, expressing binary relations between resources.

nodes.label: ontology
nodes.def: A formal explicit specification of a shared conceptualization, defining concepts, categories, properties, and relations within a domain of discourse.

nodes.label: ontology alignment
nodes.def: The result of ontology matching — a set of mappings establishing equivalence, subsumption, or other relations between aligned entities.

nodes.label: ontology engineering
nodes.def: The discipline of building, maintaining, and evolving ontologies, encompassing methodology, tools, and best practices.

nodes.label: ontology evaluation
nodes.def: The systematic assessment of ontology quality along dimensions including correctness, completeness, and coherence.

nodes.label: ontology import
nodes.def: The mechanism in OWL for one ontology to formally incorporate the axioms and declarations from another referenced ontology.

nodes.label: ontology learning
nodes.def: The automated or semi-automated extraction of ontology components from data sources such as text or structured data.

nodes.label: ontology matching
nodes.def: The automated process of finding semantic correspondences between entities from different ontologies.

nodes.label: ontology merge
nodes.def: The process of combining two or more ontologies into a unified ontology based on established alignments.

nodes.label: ontology module
nodes.def: extractable self-contained subset of an ontology that preserves semantic consistency and can be shared independently

nodes.label: ontology pattern
nodes.def: reusable solution template for modeling common domain concepts like part-whole temporal events and qualifiers

nodes.label: oauth 2 0
nodes.def: IETF RFC 6749 authorization framework enabling third-party application access to protected resources without sharing credentials; defines four grant types and token issuance via au

nodes.label: openid connect
nodes.def: Identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 (OIDC 1.0, OIDC Core spec) adding ID tokens as JWTs, userinfo endpoint, and standardized identity claims for authentication use cases.

nodes.label: access token
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 credential presented to the resource server; opaque to clients but contains or references authorization state; scoped and time-limited.

nodes.label: claims parameter
nodes.def: OIDC parameter requesting specific claims in id_token or userinfo response; server may return subset based on policy and user consent.

nodes.label: claims request object
nodes.def: Structured JSON object within the claims parameter containing claim preferences for id_token and userinfo endpoints; root container for granular claim directives.

nodes.label: token endpoint
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 endpoint accepting authorization_code or other grants and returning access_token, refresh_token, and optional id_token.

nodes.label: id token
nodes.def: OIDC JWT containing subject identifier (sub), issuer, audience, expiration, authentication event metadata, and optionally user claims; always signed.

nodes.label: refresh token
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 credential used to obtain new access tokens without re-prompting the resource owner; long-lived and tied to the same scope as the original access token.

nodes.label: resource server
nodes.def: Server hosting protected resources; validates incoming access tokens and returns resources only when tokens are valid and authorized.

nodes.label: acr claim
nodes.def: Claim in the id_token containing the ACR actually used by the OP to authenticate the user, returned to the RP

nodes.label: authorization server
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 server that authenticates the resource owner, obtains consent, and issues access tokens and optionally refresh tokens and ID tokens.

nodes.label: bearer token
nodes.def: Token type defined in RFC 6750; any party possessing the token may use it; security relies on transport TLS and token secrecy.

nodes.label: claims policy enforcement

nodes.label: expires in
nodes.def: Integer seconds indicating access token lifetime; returned alongside access_token in token response.

nodes.label: introspection endpoint
nodes.def: RFC 7662 endpoint allowing resource servers to validate access tokens; returns active status, scope, expiry, and other token metadata.

nodes.label: access token introspection

nodes.label: acr
nodes.def: Authentication Context Class: a statement about the authentication method used, the assurance level of the authentication event, and potentially the identity binding

nodes.label: acr requirement
nodes.def: A requirement statement specifying which ACRs the RP considers acceptable and in what priority order

nodes.label: acr values
nodes.def: OIDC authentication context class reference values requested by RP; ordered list the OP attempts to satisfy (e.g. 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:Password').

nodes.label: authorization endpoint
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 endpoint where the resource owner authenticates and grants consent; returns authorization_code via redirect or form_post response.

nodes.label: claims verification
nodes.def: Relying party validation that returned claims match what was requested in the claims_parameter, checking essential claims are present and values satisfy policy constraints.

nodes.label: essential claim directive
nodes.def: Claim marked as required by the relying party; identity provider must return this claim or return an error satisfying the acr_values if unable to fulfill.

nodes.label: grant type
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 parameter identifying which authorization flow is being used; values: authorization_code, client_credentials, refresh_token, password (deprecated).

nodes.label: identity provider
nodes.def: OIDC term for the authorization server that also acts as the authentication authority; issues id_token and exposes userinfo.

nodes.label: partial claims fulfillment
nodes.def: Server response state where only a subset of requested claims are returned; occurs when policy or consent excludes some claims from the request.

nodes.label: relying party
nodes.def: OIDC term for the client application that relies on the identity provider's id_token for user authentication.

nodes.label: resource indicator
nodes.def: RFC 8707 parameter specifying the target resource server URI; server issues access token scoped to that specific resource, not just the general API.

nodes.label: state
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 CSRF protection parameter; opaque string generated by the client, echoed back in the callback, and validated for binding the request and response.

nodes.label: token introspection
nodes.def: RFC 7662 introspection: protected endpoint where resource servers POST access_token to get its status, scope, expiration, and active flag.

nodes.label: userinfo endpoint
nodes.def: OIDC protected endpoint returning user claims as a JSON object; called with access_token after successful authentication; claims may overlap with id_token.

nodes.label: access denied
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 error code when the resource owner or authorization server denied the request (e.g. user clicked Deny).

nodes.label: access token audience restricted
nodes.def: RFC 8707 resource_indicator parameter scopes the access_token to a specific target resource server URI; tokens issued without resource_indicator are general-purpose and may be acce

nodes.label: access token expires in
nodes.def: Integer seconds from issuance after which the access_token is no longer valid; the resource server must reject expired tokens; returned alongside access_token in the token response

nodes.label: access token format type

nodes.label: access token hash
nodes.def: OIDC id_token at_hash claim computed as base64url(left-half(SHA256(access_token))); RP verifies to confirm access_token was not tampered with.

nodes.label: access token presented to
nodes.def: The resource_server that receives and validates the access_token on each protected API call; the token is forwarded via HTTP Authorization header using the bearer scheme.

nodes.label: access token refreshed by
nodes.def: A refresh_token is a long-lived credential optionally issued alongside the access_token that allows the client to obtain a new access_token without re-engaging the resource owner;

nodes.label: access token scope
nodes.def: The specific permission set granted to the access_token; a space-delimited string drawn from the scopes requested and approved during authorization; determines what resources and a

nodes.label: account selection required
nodes.def: OIDC error when prompt=select_account but the user has multiple accounts and must pick one.

nodes.label: achieved acr
nodes.def: The authentication context class reference actually satisfied by the OpenID Provider during an authentication event; carried in the id_token acr claim; may differ from requested_ac

nodes.label: acr claim value
nodes.def: The specific ACC URI returned in the acr claim of id_token, must be one of or satisfy the requested acr_values.

nodes.label: acr class reference
nodes.def: The URI string value that uniquely identifies a specific authentication context class; the atomic element within acr_values; examples drawn from SAML ACR URN namespace.

nodes.label: acr essential
nodes.def: OIDC parameter flag accompanying acr_values indicating whether the requested ACR is required (essential=true) or preferred; when essential=true and no acceptable ACR can be satisfi

nodes.label: acr in id token
nodes.def: The 'acr' claim embedded in the signed id_token; carries the achieved_acr identifier as a URI string; RP inspects this to verify authentication context requirements were met.

nodes.label: acr match
