nodes.label: acr mismatch
nodes.def: Identity provider condition when no requested ACC in acr_values can be satisfied, causing authentication failure per prompt=none semantics.

nodes.label: acr processing
nodes.def: The algorithmic step the OP performs upon receiving acr_values: iterate the ordered list, evaluate each acr_class against the authentication that will be performed, return the firs

nodes.label: acr satisfaction
nodes.def: The OP evaluating its authentication mechanisms against the requested ACRs and determining which ones it can satisfy

nodes.label: authentication context class
nodes.def: A named authentication context class identified by a URI string; represents a defined level of assurance or authentication method category that an Identity Provider can declare it

nodes.label: authorization code
nodes.def: Short-lived credential exchanged for tokens at the token endpoint; exists to keep tokens out of the user-agent (browser) history and address bar.

nodes.label: authorization code flow
nodes.def: Primary OAuth 2.0 flow for web apps with a server-side component; uses authorization_endpoint then token_endpoint with the returned code.

nodes.label: authorization server metadata
nodes.def: RFC 8414 metadata document at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; lists server capabilities, endpoint URLs, grant types, and supported features.

nodes.label: ciba
nodes.def: RFC 9002 Client Initiated Backchannel Authentication; user initiates auth from a device, push notification is sent to their phone, RP polls for result.

nodes.label: client
nodes.def: Application making protected resource requests on behalf of the resource owner; classified as confidential (can hold secrets) or public (cannot).

nodes.label: client credentials grant
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 flow where the client authenticates with its own credentials and receives an access token representing the client itself (no user).

nodes.label: client id
nodes.def: Public identifier assigned by the authorization server to a client; used to identify which application is requesting authorization.

nodes.label: client secret
nodes.def: Confidential credential held by the client; used with authorization_code or client_credentials flows to authenticate the client to the token endpoint.

nodes.label: device flow
nodes.def: RFC 8628 OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant; user enters a code on a separate device while the client polls for authorization completion.

nodes.label: discovery document
nodes.def: Well-known URL pattern (RFC 5785) at /.well-known/openid-configuration exposing OIDC provider configuration JSON.

nodes.label: dpop proof
nodes.def: RFC 9449 Demonstrated Proof-of-Possession; client signs a JWT with its private key and includes DPoP header in token requests to bind the token to the key.

nodes.label: id token claim target
nodes.def: Claims section of claims_request specifying which claims the relying party wants embedded directly in the signed id_token JWT.

nodes.label: id token hint
nodes.def: OIDC parameter carrying a previously issued id_token; OP uses it to infer the user and potentially skip re-authentication or pre-fill consent.

nodes.label: invalid grant
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 error code when the provided authorization grant or refresh token is invalid, expired, revoked, or already used.

nodes.label: issuer
nodes.def: String identifier (typically URL) in id_token and access_token; relying parties validate tokens were issued by a trusted, matching issuer.

nodes.label: jwks uri
nodes.def: URL in discovery document pointing to JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517) containing public keys used to verify id_token and access_token signatures.

nodes.label: login hint
nodes.def: OIDC parameter suggesting which account the user should log in with; may be email, username, or account selector hint.

nodes.label: max age
nodes.def: OIDC parameter specifying maximum seconds since last authentication; if elapsed, OP must re-authenticate before issuing id_token.

nodes.label: openid configuration
nodes.def: Discovery document served at /.well-known/openid-configuration; machine-readable metadata listing endpoints, supported features, and server capabilities.

nodes.label: pairwise identifiers
nodes.def: OIDC subject identifier strategy where each RP receives a different sub for the same user, preventing cross-RP user correlation.

nodes.label: pkce
nodes.def: RFC 7636 Proof Key for Code Exchange; mitigates authorization code interception by requiring code_verifier and code_challenge from the client.

nodes.label: prompt parameter
nodes.def: OIDC parameter controlling user interaction: none (no prompt, error if needed), login (force re-auth), consent (show approval screen), select_account.

nodes.label: pushed authorization request
nodes.def: RFC 9126 PAR: client POSTs authorization request parameters to par_endpoint first, receives request_uri for use at authorization_endpoint.

nodes.label: redirect uri
nodes.def: Callback URL the authorization server redirects to after consent; must be pre-registered with the authorization server and must match exactly.

nodes.label: resource owner
nodes.def: Entity capable of granting access to a protected resource; typically the end-user who authenticates to authorize the client's request.

nodes.label: revocation endpoint
nodes.def: RFC 7009 endpoint allowing clients to invalidate refresh or access tokens; supports bearer tokens and is advisory (server may retain copy).

nodes.label: scope
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 mechanism for requesting specific permission sets; space-delimited string (e.g. 'openid profile email'); server grants subset based on policy.

nodes.label: subject identifier
nodes.def: The 'sub' claim in id_token: a unique stable identifier assigned by the identity provider to the user; pairwise vs public based on RP.

nodes.label: token exchange
nodes.def: RFC 8693 Token Exchange grant; allows a client to exchange one token type for another (e.g. exchange a refresh token for an audience-scoped access token).

nodes.label: token type
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 parameter indicating how the access_token is to be presented to the resource server, typically Bearer, specifying the authorization scheme to use in requests.

nodes.label: ui locales
nodes.def: OIDC parameter indicating user's preferred languages for the consent/userinfo UI; BCP 47 language tag list.

nodes.label: user claims consent
nodes.def: End-user authorization for the identity provider to release specific claims; may be granted, denied, or limited compared to what relying party requested.

nodes.label: userinfo claim target
nodes.def: Claims section of claims_request specifying which claims the relying party wants returned from the userinfo_endpoint after token exchange.

nodes.label: voluntary claim directive
nodes.def: Claim requested by the relying party but not mandated; identity provider may omit based on policy, user consent, or availability without error.

nodes.label: acr request
nodes.def: The subset of an OIDC Authorization Request that specifies acr_values (and optionally acr_values essential flag); the structured representation of the RP's authentication context r

nodes.label: acr satisfaction policy
nodes.def: The internal OP policy defining how ordered acr_values list is processed to select the achieved_acr; typically returns the first class in the list that the authentication event sat

nodes.label: acr vs amr
nodes.def: The conceptual distinction that acr addresses authentication context class (what kind of assurance) while AMR addresses authentication method (how the user proved identity); acr is

nodes.label: authentication level
nodes.def: Level of Assurance semantics governing the ordering of ACC URIs in acr_values; higher-positioned ACCs imply stronger authentication requirements.

nodes.label: authentication method reference
nodes.def: The AMR claim in id_token listing specific authentication methods used (e.g. OTP, swk); distinct from acr which addresses context class; both may coexist in id_token to fully chara

nodes.label: authorization code interception
nodes.def: Threat where malware or network attacker steals the authorization code from the browser redirect; mitigated by PKCE requiring proof at token time.

nodes.label: authz code
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 authorization code: a short-lived, single-use opaque credential issued by the authorization_endpoint and exchanged at the token_endpoint for access_token and optional ref

nodes.label: back channel logout
nodes.def: OIDC Logout spec using direct server-to-server POST to RP logout endpoint; more reliable than front-channel but requires RP endpoint.

nodes.label: bearer token scheme
nodes.def: RFC 6750 token type specifying that possession of the access_token is sufficient proof of authorization; the token is transmitted in the Authorization header as 'Bearer <token>' or

nodes.label: best available ac
nodes.def: Identity provider selection rule: when acr_values lists multiple ACCs ordered by LoA, OP returns the highest ACC it can satisfy rather than failing.

nodes.label: check session iframe
nodes.def: OIDC RP iframe that polls the OP to detect changes in login state (e.g. user logged out elsewhere); enables cross-tab session sync.

nodes.label: claims supported
nodes.def: Discovery metadata field listing which claims the OP is capable of returning; clients use it to check support before requesting.

nodes.label: client assertion
nodes.def: JWT used for client authentication at the token_endpoint; signed with client's private key; contains iss, sub, aud, exp, jti claims.

nodes.label: code acr values
nodes.def: OIDC acr_values requested during authorization and stored with the code so the token endpoint can confirm the authentication context was satisfied.

nodes.label: code audience
nodes.def: The target resource or client_id for which the authorization code was issued; determines the audience claim in the resulting access_token.

nodes.label: code callback
nodes.def: The redirect_uri parameter value carried in the original authorization request and bound to the authorization_code; must match exactly at token_endpoint exchange to prevent redirec

nodes.label: code challenge
nodes.def: PKCE challenge derived from code_verifier; method S256 sends base64url(SHA256(code_verifier)); method plain sends verifier as-is.

nodes.label: code challenge method
nodes.def: PKCE parameter specifying how code_challenge was computed: S256 (SHA256 hash) or plain (plaintext); server uses same to verify.

nodes.label: code claims
nodes.def: OIDC claims_parameter values requested at authorization and preserved with the code so the userinfo endpoint or id_token reflects them.

nodes.label: code client binding
nodes.def: The authorization code is bound to the client_id that initiated the flow; the token request must authenticate as that same client using client_secret or DPoP proof.

nodes.label: code consumed at
nodes.def: Timestamp when token_endpoint successfully exchanged the authorization_code; after consumption the code becomes invalid and cannot be reused.

nodes.label: code expires in
nodes.def: Integer seconds after code_issued_at during which the authorization_code remains valid; short-lived by design to limit interception window; typically 60 seconds.

nodes.label: code expiry
nodes.def: The brief time window (typically 60 seconds) after which the authorization_code becomes invalid if not exchanged; short lifetime limits interception exposure.

nodes.label: code format
nodes.def: Server-defined structure encoding issuer, client_id, expiry, nonce, scope, and optionally the actual token claims; format is opaque to the client and may be a signed JWT.

nodes.label: code hash
nodes.def: OIDC id_token c_hash claim; analogous to at_hash but for authorization_code; verified when hybrid flow returns code from authorization_endpoint.

nodes.label: code introspection
nodes.def: RFC 7662 introspection response for a code used at the token endpoint reveals its active status, expiry, scope, and client_id before the exchange completes.

nodes.label: code issued at
nodes.def: Timestamp when authorization_server generated the authorization_code; used to enforce short-lived code_expires_in window for security.

nodes.label: code issued to
nodes.def: The client_id identifying which registered client the authorization_code was issued to; enforced at token_endpoint exchange.

nodes.label: code issuer
nodes.def: The authorization_server entity that generates and later validates the authorization_code at token exchange.

nodes.label: code nonce
nodes.def: OIDC RFC 7519 nonce parameter sent in the authorization request for implicit/hybrid flows; bound to the authorization_code so the id_token returned at token_endpoint can be correla

nodes.label: code pkce binding
nodes.def: When PKCE is active the authorization code is bound to the code_challenge presented during the authorization request; the token request must present the matching code_verifier.

nodes.label: code pkce challenge
nodes.def: The challenge derived from code_verifier and sent to authorization_endpoint during authorization request; authorization_server stores this to validate later code exchange.

nodes.label: code pkce verifier
nodes.def: The high-entropy random string (code_verifier from PKCE) required at token_endpoint to redeem authorization_code when PKCE was used in authorization request.

nodes.label: code redirect uri
nodes.def: The pre-registered redirect_uri to which authorization_server sends the authorization_code via browser redirect; must exactly match client registration.

nodes.label: code redirect uri binding
nodes.def: The redirect_uri parameter is bound to the authorization code at issuance; the redirect URI used during token exchange must match the registered URI.

nodes.label: code resource binding
nodes.def: The resource_indicator URI specified in the authorization request and attached to the authorization_code; scopes the issued access_token to that specific resource server.

nodes.label: slip card
nodes.def: A single note card serving as the atomic unit of a slip-box; the fundamental indivisible element that carries one idea.

nodes.label: knowledge management
nodes.def: The practice of systematically capturing, organizing, distilling, and expressing information to build a reusable intellectual asset base.

nodes.label: permanent notes
nodes.def: Atomic notes in Zettelkasten that exist independently of their source material; connected to other notes via explicit relationships.

nodes.label: slip box
nodes.def: Another name for Zettelkasten; emphasizes the slip-box metaphor of individual cards that can be recombined freely.

nodes.label: zettelkasten
nodes.def: A note-taking system using atomic, interconnected notes that forms a web of ideas; developed by sociologist Niklas Luhmann who wrote 70+ books using it.

nodes.label: capturing
nodes.def: The act of quickly recording any idea, insight, or information before it is lost; the first phase in the CODE framework.

nodes.label: second brain
nodes.def: A methodology and digital system for capturing, organizing, and retrieving knowledge externally so the biological brain can focus on synthesis and creativity rather than storage.

nodes.label: te organizing
nodes.def: The structuring operation that transforms captured material into a retrievable system; grouping related content by semantic relationship to enable future discovery and connection.

nodes.label: external memory
nodes.def: The second brain as an extension of biological memory; shifts the brain from storage organ to synthesis engine.

nodes.label: handwritten slip
nodes.def: A physical card with handwritten notes; the original material form Luhmann used for his 90,000-card box.

nodes.label: mental models
nodes.def: Conceptual frameworks for understanding the world; a key category of knowledge to capture and connect in a second brain.

nodes.label: te distilling
nodes.def: The process of extracting essential insights from source material through progressive summarization; a compression operation that retains meaning while reducing volume.

nodes.label: bidirectional links
nodes.def: Links that work in both directions automatically; if note A links to note B, note B sees a backlink to A without manual entry.

nodes.label: cognitive offload
nodes.def: Transferring mental tasks to external systems to free working memory for higher-order thinking; second brain is deliberate cognitive offload.

nodes.label: compounding knowledge
nodes.def: The exponential effect where each new note becomes more valuable because it can connect to and leverage the entire existing network.

nodes.label: distilling
nodes.def: Extracting essential insights from source material through progressive summarization; making information denser without losing meaning.

nodes.label: evergreen notes
nodes.def: Notes written as atomic, concept-oriented assertions that are meant to evolve over time and connect to other notes in a growing network.

nodes.label: knowledge retrieval
nodes.def: The ability to find relevant information when needed; the payoff that makes all PKM investment worthwhile.

nodes.label: literature notes
nodes.def: Notes that summarize and reflect on source material in your own words; intermediate step before permanent notes.

nodes.label: te capturing
nodes.def: The first phase of the CODE framework where information is quickly captured before it fades from working memory; a frictionless gateway that accepts raw input without requiring imm

nodes.label: te expressing
nodes.def: The final phase of the CODE framework where accumulated knowledge becomes tangible output; the conversion operation that transforms internal knowledge structures into external arti

nodes.label: atomic notes
nodes.def: Notes containing a single idea in complete, standalone form; the fundamental unit in Zettelkasten systems.

nodes.label: biological memory
nodes.def: The brain's innate memory system comprising working memory and long-term memory, subject to capacity limits and forgetting curves.

nodes.label: branching id
nodes.def: Luhmann's hierarchical ID scheme using letters and numbers (e.g., 21, 21a, 21a1) that allows new cards to be inserted between existing ones without renumbering.

nodes.label: expressing
nodes.def: Creating tangible output (articles, projects, solutions) from accumulated knowledge; the final phase where learning becomes useful.

nodes.label: knowledge graph
nodes.def: A data structure where concepts are nodes and their relationships are edges; visualized as the graph view in PKM tools.

nodes.label: networked thought
nodes.def: Thinking that occurs through and on top of a connected network of notes rather than in isolation within the biological brain.

nodes.label: note link
nodes.def: An explicit connection between two slip cards created by writing the target card's ID on the source card, forming a web of relationships.

nodes.label: physical index
nodes.def: Luhmann's topical index cards kept at the front of the box that point to entry-point card IDs by subject heading.

nodes.label: serendipity engine
nodes.def: A system designed to surface unexpected connections between ideas that you would not have found through linear search or folder browsing.

nodes.label: spaced repetition
nodes.def: A learning technique where information is reviewed at increasing intervals to optimize long-term memory retention; often used with PKM.

nodes.label: anki
nodes.def: A spaced repetition flashcard application; used alongside PKM for knowledge that needs to be memorized rather than just retrieved.

nodes.label: building a second brain
nodes.def: Tiago Forte's comprehensive methodology for externalizing thinking into a trusted digital system; based on CODE framework.

nodes.label: code framework
nodes.def: Capture, Organize, Distill, Express — the cyclical process for turning information chaos into structured creative output.

nodes.label: commonplace book
nodes.def: A historical predecessor to the Zettelkasten: a hand-copied collection of quotes, observations, and ideas from reading, used by scholars for centuries.

nodes.label: communication partner
nodes.def: Luhmann's term for treating the slip-box as a dialogue partner; asking the box questions and following links to surface unexpected connections.

nodes.label: concept mapping
nodes.def: Creating visual diagrams showing relationships between concepts; a form of externalized thinking that feeds the knowledge base.

nodes.label: creative reuse
nodes.def: Finding unexpected new applications for notes and ideas originally captured for a different purpose; enabled by networked storage.

nodes.label: deep work
nodes.def: Productive work that requires focused, undistracted attention on cognitively demanding tasks; PKM protects deep work time.

nodes.label: digital garden
nodes.def: A public-facing, evolving collection of notes that grows over time; emphasizes growth, imperfection, and learning in progress over polished publication.

nodes.label: emergence
nodes.def: Novel insights and understanding that arise from the connections between atomic notes; the whole becomes greater than the sum of parts.

nodes.label: entry point
nodes.def: A slip card serving as a hub that collects links from many other cards on a common topic, providing a navigation anchor into the box.

nodes.label: fleeting notes
nodes.def: Quick, rough captures meant to be processed and either promoted to permanent notes or discarded within a day or two.

nodes.label: graph view
nodes.def: A visual representation in PKM tools showing notes as nodes and links as edges; helps discover clusters and orphaned notes.

nodes.label: highlights
nodes.def: Selected passages from source material marked as important; raw material that must be processed through distillation into notes.

nodes.label: information architecture
nodes.def: The structural design of shared or personal information systems; PKM is personal information architecture.

nodes.label: information overload
nodes.def: The state of having more information than can be processed, leading to decision paralysis and reduced productivity; the problem PKM solves.

nodes.label: literature slip
nodes.def: A slip card that records a reference to a source text alongside or within the note, linking reading material to derived insights.

nodes.label: logseq
nodes.def: An outliner-based PKM tool with out-of-the-box bidirectional linking and daily notes; designed for long-form thinking and knowledge management.

nodes.label: luhmann
nodes.def: Niklas Luhmann, German sociologist who built the original Zettelkasten with 90,000 cards and used it to produce 70 books and 400 articles.

nodes.label: luhmann 90k cards
nodes.def: The physical Zettelkasten that Luhmann built over his lifetime; approximately 90,000 numbered index cards containing atomic ideas, arguments, and cross-references that formed his e

nodes.label: luhmann literary machine
nodes.def: Luhmann's own term for his Zettelkasten — describing it as a writing machine that generates manuscripts by navigating the card network, treating the system itself as a communicatio

nodes.label: note cluster
nodes.def: An emergent grouping of slip cards that have accumulated links around a shared theme or concept without explicit folder assignment.

nodes.label: obsidian
nodes.def: A local-first, markdown-based PKM tool with a powerful plugin ecosystem, graph view, and linking capabilities; the most popular tool for Zettelkasten-style systems.

nodes.label: org roam
nodes.def: An Emacs package that brings Zettelkasten-style bidirectional linking and knowledge graph features to org-mode.

nodes.label: organizing
nodes.def: Structuring captured material into a retrievable system; grouping related content by project, area, resource, or archive (P.A.R.A.).

nodes.label: para method
nodes.def: P.A.R.A.: Projects, Areas, Resources, Archive — a universal system for organizing any type of information by actionability.

nodes.label: progressive summarization
nodes.def: A layered note-taking technique where you progressively highlight and bold key passages across multiple passes, making notes scannable at different depths.

nodes.label: readwise
nodes.def: A service that syncs highlights from multiple sources (Kindle, Notion, etc.) and surfaces them for review via spaced repetition.

nodes.label: reference manager
nodes.def: Software for managing academic citations and source materials; integrates with PKM to provide source attribution and literature notes.

nodes.label: retrieval system
nodes.def: The mechanism by which stored information is accessed from external memory when needed; must support rapid recall and associative linking.

nodes.label: smart notes
nodes.def: Notes designed for reuse across multiple contexts with explicit connections to other notes and clear conceptual framing.

nodes.label: socratic questioning
nodes.def: Using probing questions to examine assumptions and deepen understanding; a questioning practice that generates capture-worthy reflections.

nodes.label: storage architecture
nodes.def: The organizational structure of external memory that determines how information is filed, found, and connected.

nodes.label: the intermediate holder
nodes.def: A middle layer between raw captures and final output where notes are processed, connected, and matured before use.

nodes.label: thought extender
nodes.def: A system that amplifies cognitive capacity by handling memory, organization, and retrieval so the brain can operate at higher levels.

nodes.label: working memory
nodes.def: The limited-capacity cognitive workspace where active thinking occurs; the primary target for cognitive offload via external memory systems.

nodes.label: writing to think
nodes.def: The practice of using writing as a cognitive tool to clarify thinking, discover new ideas, and work through complex problems.

nodes.label: zettelkasten method
nodes.def: The specific methodology of writing index cards with one idea each, numbering them to allow linking, and building an external thinking system.

nodes.label: accumulation
nodes.def: The organic growth process of a slip-box over time; cards added gradually form an increasingly dense network of linked ideas.

nodes.label: archivierung
nodes.def: Luhmann's filing and archival approach to the slip-box; the systematic process of assigning IDs, linking cards, and maintaining the growing network.

nodes.label: associative thinking
nodes.def: The cognitive process of making unexpected connections between disparate ideas; enabled and amplified by a networked knowledge system.

nodes.label: attention as scarcity
nodes.def: The perspective that human attention is the rarest resource, so PKM should optimize for retrieval speed not just capture volume.

nodes.label: attention as scarcy
nodes.def: Attention is a finite, exhaustible resource that must be deliberately allocated; because attention is scarce, every cognitive overhead consumed by remembering, organizing, or track

nodes.label: backlinks
nodes.def: Bidirectional links where referencing a note automatically creates a visible reference back; core to networked thought tools.

nodes.label: bidirectional link
nodes.def: A note link recorded on both participating cards, ensuring navigability in both directions through the slip-box network.

nodes.label: block references
nodes.def: Links to specific chunks or paragraphs of content rather than entire documents; enables granular knowledge reuse.

nodes.label: box context
nodes.def: The container holding all slip cards plus the index; the physical or digital environment where the network of ideas resides.

nodes.label: card id
nodes.def: A unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to each slip card enabling explicit reference and bidirectional linking within the box.

nodes.label: card writing habit
